root_cause: Direct CLI drives (audio/render/gates/cut) move the job to an active state via jobs.transition(), which clears the lease fields on every move. On drive failure (_die/CliError or an unexpected traceback) the job sat in aligning/rendering/gating/cutting with a NULL lease. claim() only reclaims active jobs whose lease is non-NULL and expired, and no CLI path exits those states - so the job was unclaimable and unrecoverable without SQL. The work loop was already safe (T-003: except Exception -> queue.fail()); only the direct-drive commands were exposed.
